newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes stagnant on first day for June prompts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes stagnant on first day for June prompts.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices were stagnant on Monday, with volumes thinned for the first day of June prompt cash trading.
Outright prices moved to slightly lower ranges, deflated by technical selling in a quiet market.
June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was around 5 cents lower $19.90-20.00 a barrel, with second month July also pegged at the same price levels.
Grade business saw both sweet and sour barrels talk at weaker levels than May did late last week, led by Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James at steady to 10 cts under WTI.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was talked at a wide 50-70 cts discount to the benchmark.
Midland/WTI moved 25-30 cts cheaper than the June WTI/Cushing.
For the sours, West Texas Sour/Midland was offered at $1.70 under the marker, with bids at to more than $1.80 under the mark.
Eugene Island was barely talked at a $1.60 discount to the marker.
June Postings Plus was at a wide $1.65-75, moving in-line with the steady Jun/Jul WTI spread.
